subject: Geography
central_question: How do direct materials, seismic waves and other indirect evidence reveal the structure and processes of earth’s inaccessible interior?
in_scope_units: Direct and indirect sources of information about earth’s interior.
Earthquakes, faults, focus, epicentre and seismic waves.
Propagation of P, S and surface waves and shadow zones.
Crust, mantle, asthenosphere, lithosphere and core.
banned_topics: Detailed plate-boundary theory, which belongs to Distribution of Oceans and Continents.
Origin of the universe, which belongs to The Origin and Evolution of the Earth.
Detailed weathering and erosion, which belong to Geomorphic Processes.

known_pitfalls.claim: Scientists have travelled to earth’s centre.
known_pitfalls.correction: Most deep knowledge comes from indirect evidence because direct access is extremely limited.

known_pitfalls.claim: P and S waves travel through all materials alike.
known_pitfalls.correction: P-waves pass through solids and fluids; S-waves pass only through solids.

known_pitfalls.claim: Focus and epicentre are the same point.
known_pitfalls.correction: The focus is inside earth; the epicentre is directly above it on the surface.

known_pitfalls.claim: The lithosphere is only the crust.
known_pitfalls.correction: It includes the crust and rigid uppermost mantle.
Some cools underground as intrusive bodies.

recommended_example_progression: Use Exercise 2(ii) to distinguish direct sources.
Use Exercise 2(iii) to explain the shadow zone.
Use Exercise 3(i) to explain wave effects on rock masses.
Use Exercise 3(ii) to describe intrusive forms.
